program.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
requirements.source_phrase: Move the mug to the right of the headphones

outcomes.description: Move the mug so that it is positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.target: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.reference: The headphones in the image; compare the mug’s position with the headphones.

nodes.question: Is the source mug visibly positioned to the right of the same headphones in the edited image; if not, is there reliable visual evidence of relevant attempted movement of the source mug, or reliable evidence that no relevant progress occurred?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when visual evidence reliably establishes that the source mug itself is now positioned to the right of the same headphones. Fail when visual evidence reliably establishes either that relevant attempted movement occurred without fulfillment, or that no relevant progress toward the requested move occurred. For attempted movement, assess the source mug's former location and surrounding edited scene together; a conspicuous remnant or other visible changes may support attempted movement even if the right-side mug's identity cannot be established. Do not infer source-mug identity or fulfillment from color alone, from a mug being on the right, or from unrelated/newly generated mugs. A remnant counts as evidence of attempted movement only when its shape, position, and appearance reliably connect it to the source mug or otherwise clearly indicate a relevant edit. Use unknown when evidence cannot reliably establish fulfillment, attempted movement, or absence of progress. High confidence in uncertainty is not evidence that the requested edit is absent.
nodes.binding: Compare the source image's large light-blue mug, including its body and handle, with the edited mugs, allowing for changes in appearance, scale, and lighting; compare the same headphones and assess whether the source mug is to their right. Separately inspect the source mug's former location and surrounding edited scene for reliable evidence of attempted movement, including the remnant's position, outline, and appearance and any other visible changes. Do not treat color alone, an indistinct blur, or a different-looking mug as proof of source-mug identity or progress. Keep attempted movement distinct from fulfillment: attempted movement without fulfillment is fail for this required condition; retain unknown if neither fulfillment nor relevant progress/no-progress can reliably be established.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d1: The trace correctly identifies attempted movement but its fail status conflates that with the node’s fulfillment check: the criterion explicitly says attempted movement without fulfillment is fail, so the reference partial is not a reason to force pass. However, the binding asks whether there is evidence of no progress, which can bias the decision toward a binary no and obscure the rubric’s partial-progress distinction. Make the decision output/criterion explicitly distinguish fulfillment, reliable attempted movement without fulfillment, reliable absence of progress, and unresolved evidence, then ensure the aggregate maps the observed attempted-move case to partial rather than treating this single requirement’s fail as overall no. In these images, the source mug is large and light blue; the edited right-side mug is small and white, so identity/fulfillment is unestablished, while a conspicuous blue mug-shaped remnant at the former location supports attempted movement. Preserve that evidence without treating color alone as identity. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; the mismatch is in decision-to-aggregate semantics, not missing visual evidence.

observations.evidence: The edited image shows the same headphones near the center and a mug to their right, but that mug is small and white, unlike the source's large light-blue mug, so its identity is not established. At the source mug's former left-side location there is a conspicuous light-blue, mug-shaped blur/remnant, while the original mug is absent there. Together these visible changes reliably indicate an attempted move, but do not establish that the source mug itself is now to the headphones' right.

findings.source_phrase: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
findings.question: Does the mug on the right in the edited image reliably appear to be the source mug, despite its changed appearance, or is it a different/new mug?
findings.criteria: Compare the source mug’s body, handle, and other visible features with the right-side edited mug, allowing for appearance changes. Do not infer identity from position alone. Record whether the visual evidence supports source-mug identity, a different mug, or remains inconclusive.
findings.evidence: The source shows one large light-blue mug left of the headphones. The edited image has a small light-blue blur at the former location, a white mug near the headphones, and another white mug to their right. The saved observation says the right-side mug’s identity is not established, but does not separately examine whether either white mug’s shape or handle provides evidence of continuity with the source mug.
findings.rationale: The existing check identifies the central uncertainty as source-mug identity. A focused comparison of the right-side mug’s visible features against the source mug could clarify whether the requested placement is fulfilled or whether the apparent right-side mug is unrelated; the blur and extra mug make this worth investigating without presuming either conclusion.

transactions.reason: The single required condition currently treats attempted movement as a failed requirement, so deterministic counting labels the edit “no” despite visible partial progress. Split the condition into fulfillment and relevant-progress checks: fulfillment remains the sole pass condition, while the progress check distinguishes attempted movement from reliable absence of progress. This preserves the requirement and lets the existing all/some/none count represent partial progress without encoding a reference label.

decisions.criteria: Pass only when visual evidence reliably establishes that the source mug itself is now positioned to the right of the same headphones. Fail when visual evidence reliably establishes that the source mug is not positioned to their right, including when a right-side mug cannot reliably be identified as the source mug. Use unknown when the evidence cannot reliably establish whether the source mug is positioned to the right. Do not infer source-mug identity or fulfillment from color or position alone, or from unrelated/newly generated mugs.

Compare the same headphones and determine whether the source mug is visibly to their right. Do not treat color alone, an indistinct blur, or a different-looking mug as proof of source-mug identity. Fail only when visual evidence reliably establishes that no relevant progress toward the requested move occurred. A remnant supports attempted movement only when its shape, position, and appearance reliably connect it to the source mug or otherwise clearly indicate a relevant edit; do not infer progress from color alone, an indistinct blur, or an unrelated mug.

Compare the source mug's body and handle with edited objects, allowing for appearance changes.
